national_review_question: Across Medicare, how do coverage rules, payment values, cost sharing and administrative requirements affect access to clinically indicated care for women and men, including unequal effects of formally neutral rules?
motivating_example_rule: Estradiol is one motivating case in a national review of drugs, procedures and care pathways; a single drug finding cannot establish or resolve the national question.
medicare_benchmark_rule: Medicare is the national policy benchmark for care in later life and substantial health needs, not a claim that it finances most US care or that most lifetime care occurs after 65. Preserve younger Medicare beneficiaries separately. See research/medicare_benchmark.json for the rationale, age-stratification and measurement rules.
topic_scope: Sex-specific conditions, conditions predominantly affecting one sex, and shared conditions across reproductive, sexual, cardiovascular, cancer, musculoskeletal, pain, mental health, preventive and rehabilitative care.
comparison_rule: Use within-condition comparisons, clinically justified service groups and population-burden analyses. Do not require a direct counterpart for every sex-specific service. Consider utilization and service mix as possible mechanisms as well as confounders.
policy_level_rule: Distinguish Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage and Part D; national rules, contractor decisions and plan implementation; preserve policy year and denominators.
scope_decision: Exclude transgender-focused patient evidence and gender-affirming care from the present review and future white paper.
mixed_population_rule: Use only separately extractable eligible cisgender male/female results from mixed-population studies. Exclude nonseparable mixed results from the primary synthesis and record the reason.
unreported_identity_rule: Studies reporting only male/female remain candidate evidence pending full-text eligibility checks. Record gender identity as not reported; do not infer confirmed cisgender status or zero transgender participants.
nonpatient_data_rule: Fee schedules, formularies and policy documents have no patient cohort. Retain when relevant to included indications and label as policy or code-level evidence.
clinical_basis_rule: Separate shared body systems, female/male reproductive anatomy, female/male reproductive physiology and mixed or site-dependent services. Classify each indication rather than the molecule or assumed patient identity. Keep sex-defined eligibility and disease burden distinct. Classification details are in research/clinical_basis.json.
anatomy_analysis_rule: Compare women and men within shared conditions when clinically comparable. For anatomy- or physiology-linked care, assess need, benefit and policy consistency without requiring an opposite-sex counterpart. Split bundled services by organ, indication and procedure before comparative synthesis.

G06.comparison: Mammography and other cancer screening: compare eligibility and patient costs while accounting for different clinical indications.
G06.disparity_evidence: The previously linked transgender-screening studies are excluded under the revised population criterion. No eligible screening-disparity study is currently linked.
G06.evidence_type: National coverage policy; in-scope literature gap
G06.limitations: Screening and diagnostic mammography have different coverage rules. A difference between screening programs is not itself proof of bias.
G06.next_question: Identify eligible studies of screening costs, denials and follow-up among women and clinically justified comparisons.
